findings.title: User-level download/upload over plain HTTP with no authentication (MITM-injectable game content)
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/get_level.php";
public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/save_level.php";
findings.entry_point: Automatic background download at startup: ApoImpPanel.init -> loadUserlevels() spawns a Thread (ApoImpPanel.java:78-81, 204-212) -> ApoImpUserlevels.loadUserlevels() -> ApoImpUserlevelsLoad.load(). Upload path: editor Upload button -> ApoImpEditor.uploadString() -> ApoImpUserlevels.addLevel() -> ApoImpUserlevelsLoad.save()
findings.sink: urlConn = url.openConnection(); ... printout.writeBytes(content); ... input = new DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()) in ApoImpUserlevelsLoad.save (lines 123-143) and load (lines 164-210)
findings.data_path: Startup thread calls ApoImpUserlevelsLoad.load(), which opens http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/get_level.php, POSTs "Get=", then reads the response line-by-line into 11 parallel ArrayLists (level string + metadata). Every 11th line (i%11==0) is stored verbatim as a level string in this.levels, later copied into ApoImpLevel.editorLevels (ApoImpUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted, line 28/48). Uploads POST "level=<raw string>" unencrypted.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (or any DNS/network hijack of www.apo-games.de, no TLS so no warning possible) answers get_level.php with crafted rows whose numeric columns are digits but whose i%11==0 'level' lines are hostile payloads (see ApoImp-02). The payload is fetched automatically at game start; the victim just clicks the 'userlevels' menu button and the malformed level is parsed, crashing the game. Uploaded levels can equally be stripped/replaced in transit, poisoning the shared level pool.
findings.preconditions: ApoConstants.B_ONLINE == true (hardcoded true, org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:16); attacker needs an active network position (MITM/DNS/spoofed host) since traffic is cleartext port 80.
findings.validation_plan: Run the game while capturing with `tcpdump -A port 80` orWireshark: startup shows a cleartext POST to /apoElf/get_level.php and clicking Upload shows POST body 'level=<digits>'. Then redirect www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 via /etc/hosts, serve a stub PHP that echoes 11-line groups with valid integers and a malicious level line (e.g. 100 chars, see ApoImp-02), and observe the client accept it without any certificate/trust error.

findings.title: Hand-rolled level parser performs unchecked length/geometry arithmetic on server-controlled level strings, crashing the game thread
findings.code_excerpt: level = new int[(l.length() / 14 + 2) * 2][16]; ... char c = l.charAt(y * 14 + x); level[y+1][x+1] = Integer.valueOf(c) - 48; ... level[y + 16 + addFall][x] = addFall * 30;
findings.entry_point: Server response line stored as level string (ApoImpUserlevelsLoad.load, i%11==0, line 186) -> ApoImpLevel.editorLevels -> ApoImpGame.loadLevel(boolean) line 210 picks it -> loadLevel(bEditor, l) line 226. Local analog: clipboard paste via VK_L (lines 108-118), but that call site wraps parsing in try/catch.
findings.sink: l.charAt(y*14+x) (line 232), Integer.valueOf(c)-48 (line 233), fall-simulation write level[y+16+addFall][x] (line 297), render read level[y+16][x] (line 563), and goal sentinel lookup level[goalY][goalX] with goalX/goalY==-1 when no '4' tile exists (lines 421/476)
findings.data_path: loadLevel(boolean,String) sizes the grid purely from string length ((len/14+2)*2 rows) and accepts ANY character as a cell value ('a' becomes 49). No validation that len%14==0, that a goal tile exists, or that piece/fall geometry keeps indices in range. The call chain loadNextLevel->loadLevel has no try/catch, and the engine loop ApoSubGame.run() (org/apogames/ApoSubGame.java:88-132) has no catch-all around think()/render(), so the first RuntimeException terminates the whole game thread.
findings.attack_scenario: 1) Attacker MITMs get_level.php (see ApoImp-01) and returns numeric metadata plus a level line of 100 characters. On 'userlevels' play, (100/14+2)*2=18 rows are allocated but the parse loop reads up to index 111 -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in loadLevel, uncaught -> ApoSubGame thread dies, window freezes. 2) Alternatively a syntactically fitting level with no '4' goal tile leaves goalX/goalY=-1 and the first think() tick hits level[-1][-1] at line 476 -> ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Impact is reliable client-side denial of service of the game process's logic thread; no code execution.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE true and network position to inject the HTTP response (remote case), or local user pastes a malformed string themselves (then partially guarded by try/catch at ApoImpGame.java:112-117).
findings.validation_plan: Stub get_level.php with: integer filler lines plus one level line of exactly 100 chars of '1'. Start game, press the userlevels button; console shows StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from apoImp.game.ApoImpGame.loadLevel and the game stops updating (thread death). Repeat with a 196-char grid containing no '4' to trigger the AIOOBE at line 476 on the first tick.

findings.title: Cloned ApoClassLoader instantiates classes from file:/http: URLs (defineClass-equivalent) - dead code in this variant
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); ... c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); ... return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: repo-wide grep finds zero references to ApoClassLoader outside its own file (the AI-opponent-loading feature it serves was cloned in from siblings but is never invoked by ApoImpMain/ApoImpApplet).
findings.sink: cl.loadClass(classname) followed by c.newInstance() (lines 73-75) - arbitrary bytecode from any file path or URL passed to the constructor is defined and instantiated with full permissions of the JVM.
findings.data_path: Theoretical only: getMyClass() turns getPath() into a File.toURI().toURL() (application mode, line 66) or new URL(path) (applet mode, line 68) and executes whatever class is found there. Had it been wired up (as in sibling variants that load .class 'AI' opponents), any local file the user can be talked into selecting, or any HTTP URL in applet mode, would yield direct code execution.
findings.attack_scenario: Not exploitable as shipped: no call site. Documented because the identical class IS reachable in sibling variants of the corpus; if a future clone re-attaches it, an attacker who controls the selected path/URL gains arbitrary native Java code execution under the user's account.
findings.preconditions: Requires someone to reintroduce a caller (e.g. the JFileChooser-based AI loader skeleton still present but unused in ApoImpComponent.java:66-73).
findings.validation_plan: Static proof of unreachability: `grep -rn ApoClassLoader _from_jar_ApoImp` matches only the class itself. Dynamic proof of dangerousness if ever called: place a class with a static initializer printing 'pwned' under a temp dir, construct new ApoClassLoader(tmpdir, 'Pwn').getMyClass() in a scratch main and observe execution.

findings.title: MD5 helper and plaintext-HTTP highscore submission machinery present but unreferenced (dead cloned infra)
findings.code_excerpt: MessageDigest lDigest = MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"); lDigest.update(pInput.getBytes()); BigInteger lHashInt = new BigInteger(1, lDigest.digest());
findings.entry_point: None: getMd5Digest has zero callers in this variant; likewise ApoHighscore.save/load (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:73/122), ApoGameCounter.save (help/ApoGameCounter.java:36), ApoHelp.saveData/loadData cookies.php (ApoHelp.java:473/505) and AudioPlayer's http://www.apo-games.de/apoPongBeat fetch (sound/AudioPlayer.java:68) are never reached from game code.
findings.sink: MD5 digest used as integrity/validation primitive (line 286-289); ApoHighscore.load additionally parses the server response with Integer.valueOf/Float.valueOf per line (lines 151-163) catching only IOException, so a malicious server line would throw an uncaught NumberFormatException had the code been wired.
findings.data_path: In sibling variants these classes implement the score-submission/validation flow over http://www.apo-games.de/apoSheeptastic/save_highscore.php (constants at org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:21-28). Here ApoImp ships them as inert copies - no highscore UI exists, so no name/score ever leaves the machine.
findings.attack_scenario: No scenario as shipped. If re-wired (clone propagation risk): a network attacker could forge scores (MD5-over-plaintext, no secret), spoof leaderboard contents served over HTTP, and crash clients with non-numeric lines.
findings.preconditions: A caller must be reintroduced; today B_ONLINE=true alone is not enough because nothing invokes ApoHighscore/ApoGameCounter.
findings.validation_plan: `grep -rn 'ApoHighscore\|getMd5Digest\|ApoGameCounter\|AudioPlayer' _from_jar_ApoImp/apoImp` returns no matches - proving the sinks are inert in this clone while present in siblings; use for cross-variant diffing of where they become live.

findings.title: Shared-level upload endpoint trusts the client completely (no auth, no validation, raw content relay)
findings.sink: POST of the raw level string to http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/save_level.php (lines 123-137); the only 'check' is a duplicate-suppression equals() loop client-side (ApoImpUserlevels.java:80-84)
findings.data_path: The client serializes whatever grid the local editor holds (getLevelString, ApoImpEditor.java:102-115) and POSTs it with no session token, signature, or rate limiting visible in the protocol; the server is expected to validate. Combined with ApoImp-01 (cleartext), anyone can also inject uploads without even running the game.
findings.attack_scenario: A user (or MITM replaying the form-urlencoded POST) floods the shared level database with garbage or oversized strings; other clients auto-download them at startup (ApoImp-01) and parse them (ApoImp-02), so a single poisoned upload griefs every player's level browser and can freeze their game threads. Gained: vandalism/DoS of the community content channel; no per-user accountability.
findings.preconditions: Network access to www.apo-games.de (port 80); nothing else - the request carries no credential.
findings.validation_plan: curl -X POST -d 'level=00000000000000...' http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/save_level.php and then reload the in-game userlevels list (restart client or click upload flow) to confirm the injected entry appears; demonstrates the endpoint accepts unauthenticated arbitrary content. (Live-endpoint test only if the server still exists; otherwise reproduce against a local stub.)

findings.title: Unbounded line-by-line ingestion of server responses into memory lists
findings.code_excerpt: while (null != ((str = input.readLine()))) { if (i % 11 == 0) { this.levels.add(str); } else if (i % 11 == 1) { this.times.add(Float.valueOf(str)); } ... }
findings.entry_point: Automatic startup thread ApoImpPanel.loadUserlevels() -> ApoImpUserlevels.loadUserlevels() -> load() reading the HTTP response body
findings.sink: Unbounded readLine() loop appending every response line into 11 ArrayLists (lines 184-209); identical pattern in dead code ApoHighscore.load lines 151-164
findings.data_path: Server (or MITM per ApoImp-01) streams an arbitrarily large/infinite response; each line is retained verbatim (level strings) or boxed (Integer/Float), with no cap on element count, line length, or total bytes. Heap fills until OutOfMemoryError on the loader thread; the surrounding try/catch(Exception) in ApoImpUserlevels.java:32 catches Error? No - OutOfMemoryError is an Error, so it escapes and can take down the loader thread/VM state mid-parse.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker answering get_level.php streams ~1 GB of '1' lines; the game (which fetches automatically on launch) allocates until heap exhaustion, degrading or killing the client. Gained: reliable client resource exhaustion from a network position.
findings.preconditions: Active MITM/DNS control of the get_level.php response (origin server is trusted-ish); default JVM heap sizes suffice.
findings.validation_plan: Point www.apo-games.de at a netcat/python stub that emits '1\n' forever after consuming the POST body; launch the game with -Xmx256m and watch RSS climb until OutOfOfMemoryError appears on the userlevel loader thread.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere in the tree

path_traversal - no user-controlled filesystem path reaches File APIs in live code; the JFileChooser in ApoImpComponent.getFileChooser (ApoImpComponent.java:66-73) is never called, and ApoIO/ApoCopy file helpers have zero callers; levels travel via the system clipboard, not disk files
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, or keys exist in the variant
information_disclosure - only local System.getProperty("user.language") read (ApoImpConstants.java:22), never transmitted; no PII leaves the machine in live code paths

legacy_sandbox_assumption - present as design residue rather than vulnerability: JApplet entry (ApoImpApplet.java:18-29) sets B_APPLET and gates clipboard/file access (ApoHelp.java:300/314, ApoImpGame.java:109), but the sandbox itself imposes no additional risk today since applets no longer run
notes: This variant is effectively a re-skinned clone of ApoElf: PROGRAM_NAME = "=== ApoElf ===" and the menu renders 'ApoElf' (ApoImpConstants.java:29, ApoImpMenu.java:57), and it uploads/downloads shared levels to the apoElf directory (/apoElf/get_level.php, ApoImpConstants.java:15-16) while the copied org.apogames.ApoConstants still points at /apoSheeptastic/ endpoints (ApoConstants.java:21-28) - textbook clone-and-own constant drift that matters for the corpus study: flaws propagate wholesale, including mismatched endpoints. Roughly half of the shared org.apogames infrastructure (ApoClassLoader, ApoHighscore, ApoGameCounter, ApoHelp.saveData/loadData, ApoIO, ApoCopy, the entire sound package incl. AudioPlayer's remote MP3 fetch, image scaling tools) is dead code here - verified by reference greps - so the corpus-wide patterns those files embody are latent, not live, in ApoImp. The only genuinely live network surface is the userlevel get/save pair, and the only live 'parser' attack surface is the 14-characters-per-row level-string format, which is also exchanged through the system clipboard (editor save copies it out, VK_L pastes it in - ApoImpEditor.java:246, ApoImpGame.java:110-114); the clipboard route is defensively wrapped in try/catch while the server route is not. There are no save games, replays, or local config files in this variant.
